entries.alt: The Plugins page of the administration console with the registered plugins, their trust, whether they are running and their approval, and the Register a plugin button.
The Webhooks tab of Integrations with one outbound and one inbound webhook listed above the Add a webhook form.
The AI assistant page of the administration console: the running status, the endpoint, the capabilities, the data limits, the rate limit and the provider profiles.
The UI plugins page listing one registered plugin with its signature state and its approval.
The setting Background push notifications allowed in the console's Settings, with its value for the whole server, per domain and per user.
The Branding screen of the administration console, with the product name and sign-in notice at the top and one section for each image.
The Package tracking screen of the console with the AfterShip provider form.
The Composer features card in the Settings screen.
The Register a plugin form with the Component choice, the plugin id, and the capabilities and hosts fields.
The page of the Rspamd plugin with markers on Status, Granted capabilities, Network and limits and Spam classifier.
The Add a webhook form for an outbound webhook, with markers on the direction, the account, the URL and the Create webhook button.
The secret of a new webhook, hidden here, with the line saying it is not shown again, how deliveries are signed, and the button I have copied it.
The Overview tab of Observability: the tab strip, the period control, notes about what the figures mean, and the first key figures for traffic and client load times.
The six tabs of Observability with markers 1 to 6: Overview, Audit log, Configure operational telemetry, Client errors, Database and Resources.
The Client load times group of key figures: median, 95th and 99th percentile for time to usable, first contentful paint, largest contentful paint and page load, with the number of samples under each.
A new message with the composer ribbon open on the Format text tab.
The Outbox screen with one message waiting to send, its status, its Send now, Recall and edit and Cancel buttons, and the Outbox count in the folder list.
The Endpoint group of the AI assistant page: endpoint type, base URL, the stored API key, and the chat, embedding and speech-to-text models.
The Rate limit group of the AI assistant page with the text that the server applies only MW_ASSIST_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN and the Requests per minute field.
The Provider profiles section of the AI assistant page with no profiles yet and the Add profile button.
The View group of the composer ribbon opened, showing the Dark background button and the Editor zoom selector.
The Send later menu under the arrow beside Send: In 1 hour, Later today 17:00, Tomorrow morning 09:00, Monday morning 09:00 and Pick date and time.
The Drafts list of the composer with the Account drafts tab selected and one account draft, marked Open now and Account.
The setting Push quiet hours in the console's Settings.
The top of the Saved statistics card on the Observability Overview, with markers 1 and 2 on the range buttons and the Saved badge with the row count.
The Most frequent not-found paths table: each row has the method, the redacted path and a count, with the app's own clients listed apart from other traffic.
The Client errors tab: filters for status, build, location and age, buttons to export CSV or JSON, and a table of two error groups.
The Authentication logs tab of Logs: the filter form and a table of sign-in attempts with area, backend, result, reason, method and source address.
The filter form of the Authentication logs with markers 1 to 6 on the search box, Sign-in area, Result, Backend, Reason and Apply filters.
The Application logs tab: a note on what is captured, the count of discarded entries, search, component and severity filters, and warnings captured since the server started.
The Overview tab of Diagnostics after Run all checks: one tile per group with counts of OK, warning, failed and not run checks, and the Needs attention list.
The eight tabs of Diagnostics with markers 1 to 8: Overview, Server, Connectivity, Mail backends, Security posture, Tools, History and Report.

The Security posture tab of Diagnostics after a run: rows for HTTPS, secure cookies, HSTS, CSRF protection and the other posture checks, each with a status chip, its result and, for a warning, how to fix it.
The Maintenance mode tab: a status line saying webmail is accepting requests, the Pause user access switch, a message box, the retry delay and Save.

fill.label: @maintenance-mode-message
fill.value: Mail is paused until 14:00 UTC while the database is repaired.

entries.alt: The Maintenance mode form with markers 1 to 4 on the Pause user access switch, the message for users with a sample text, the retry delay and Save.
The Database tab of Maintenance: online SQLite conversion, retained databases, and background database maintenance with Configure maintenance and Run a batch.
The Offline database repair card on the Repair jobs tab: the preview and apply commands with a Copy command button each, and the optional flags.
The Database tab of Observability: file size, occupied pages, reusable space and write-ahead log size, with connection details and pool usage below.
Configuration and backups with the Export settings tab open: a note on what portable files contain, three tabs, and the Download settings button.

The Settings backups to Nextcloud form: server URL, username, app password, target folder, copies to keep, keep days and private certificate authority, with Save destination, Test connection and Back up now.
The Hosting panels page under Integrations: the description, the New hosting connection button, and the empty list.
The New hosting connection form: connection name, provider, HTTPS panel origin, credential choice, connection route and TLS options.
The Server metadata page: an Account selector and the prompt to select an account before its annotations are shown.
The Effective configuration page: the search and filter row and a table of settings with their reported value, source and how a change applies.
The Register a UI plugin form with a manifest pasted in and the preview of what the manifest declares.
The search and filter row of Effective configuration with markers 1 to 3 on Search configuration, Area and Source.
The Name and sign-in notice section of the Branding screen, with the product name and the sign-in notice filled in.
The Logo section: a thumbnail of the current image, the file chooser and the Restore default button.
The Maskable installed app icon (512 px) section, with its size and 80 percent circle guidance.
The AfterShip Tracking card: a checkbox to allow opted-in accounts to contact the provider, the provider API key field and the minimum refresh interval, set to 900 seconds.

The top of the Composer features card: the Applies to and Profiles selectors, the Apply profile button and the first feature row with its Value and Lock for users checkboxes and the Use default button.
The Settings screen searched for mail.send, listing the undo-send window, its maximum, the recall switch, the scheduling horizon and the queue size.
The Settings screen searched for receipt, listing the read receipt, delivery notification and scheduled receipt settings.
The Settings screen searched for mailer, showing the Remove outgoing mailer headers setting switched on by default.
The top row of the composer: Send and its Send later arrow on the left, and Discard, Save to Drafts, Drafts and Recall on the right, numbered 1 to 6.
The notice after pressing Send: Message queued, the time left to undo, and the Undo and Send now buttons.
One message in the Outbox, marked Sending soon, with its Send now, Recall and edit and Cancel buttons numbered 1 to 3.
The Mailing list dialog for City Library News: the list name, List-Id and sender, the ways to unsubscribe, and buttons including Unsubscribe and Always keep, numbered 1 to 3.
